Figure 3. ECG classification performance across age groups. (A) The older-adult model was tested unchanged on independently collected young-adult and older-adult ECGs. (B–C) Three training approaches were compared in children and infants: adapting an older-adult model, adapting a young-adult model, and training a new model using pediatric data alone. All approaches used the same pediatric training patients. Test patients were kept separate from training and model adjustment. Earlier older-adult training improved performance in children, while infant results remained uncertain. The pediatric study used five rounds of patient-level testing on previously examined data. Its uncertainty ranges describe the fitted models and do not include variation from repeating the full training process.
